conceptual assets.information: The operational enable setting determines whether the one-wire engine, its FIFOs, and the exported clock-enable function are active. The setting is received through the bus and returned in the control read-back.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: A bus write changes the enable at line 142, while the setting controls FIFO clearing and serial operation at lines 199, 231, and 311, so unauthorized modification can corrupt operation. Clearing or disabling the setting suppresses the exported clock enable at line 273 and can stop transfers by clearing both FIFOs at lines 199 and 231.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker able to write the control register could clear or disable the engine, preventing queued one-wire transfers and clock generation.

conceptual assets.information: The clear control requests clearing of the transmit and receive buffering. The one-wire engine depends on those buffers retaining queued commands and received results.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: A bus write stores the clear control at line 143, and it directly controls both FIFO clear inputs at lines 199 and 231, allowing unauthorized clearing or alteration of buffered information. Asserting the control can discard queued commands or received results through the FIFO clear paths at lines 199 and 231, withholding required transfers.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could issue a control write that asserts clear and erases pending transmit or receive data.

conceptual assets.information: The prescaler and divider settings determine the rate of the internal one-wire timing ticks used by serial transfers. The settings are needed for correctly timed one-wire communication and are returned in the control read-back.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Bus writes modify the prescaler and divider at lines 144 and 145, and those values control tick generation at lines 260 and 261, so unauthorized changes can produce incorrect transfer timing. A modified divider or prescaler can suppress or badly space the ticks required by the serial engine at lines 360 and 366, preventing communication.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could program an invalid prescaler or divider so one-wire bits are sampled or driven at the wrong rate.

conceptual assets.information: The command field selects the one-wire operation, such as bit, byte, reset, or no operation. The serial engine depends on this command to select the waveform and operation state.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The command is written into the transmit FIFO through line 201 and selects the serial state and operation at lines 331 through 335, so unauthorized modification can cause an incorrect one-wire operation. A changed command can select a no-op or reset path instead of the requested transfer, withholding or disrupting the output at lines 300 and 302.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter a queued command so the engine emits a reset, no-op, or wrong transfer type.

conceptual assets.information: The payload byte written by the bus is queued and shifted onto the one-wire output during bit or byte operations. The one-wire transfer depends on this payload being retained and emitted unchanged.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The payload enters the transmit FIFO at line 201 and influences the serial output at lines 328, 342, 300, and 302, so an unauthorized observer of the one-wire line can expose it. Unauthorized modification of the bus-written payload at line 201 or its serial use at line 328 can cause an incorrect transmitted value. Clearing or disabling the transmit path at lines 199 and 231 can discard or withhold the payload before it reaches the output.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could observe the one-wire output, alter a queued payload, or clear the transmit FIFO before the payload is sent.

conceptual assets.information: The byte sampled from the one-wire input is shifted into a receive result and queued for software read-back. The receive path depends on preserving the sampled byte until it is returned through the bus response.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The received value enters from the one-wire input at line 296 and is exposed through the bus response at lines 161 and 162, providing a path for unauthorized disclosure. An altered one-wire input can change the sampled result at lines 296 and 352, compromising the integrity of the returned byte. Clearing the receive FIFO at line 231 or consuming its data through line 234 can cause a required received result to be lost or withheld.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could monitor the bus read-back, drive a false one-wire value, or clear the receive FIFO before software reads the result.

conceptual assets.information: The presence result records whether a one-wire device responded during the reset-presence interval. Software depends on this result in the receive word to determine whether a device is present.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The result is computed from the sampled one-wire input at line 375 and returned in the response at line 162, so an altered input or internal result can make software report the wrong device presence.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter the sampled one-wire response or the stored presence result so software accepts or rejects a device incorrectly.

conceptual assets.information: The interrupt request reports that the enabled engine has no queued transmit work and is not busy. An interrupt-driven integrator may depend on this event to service or continue transfers.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The interrupt output is produced from enable, transmit availability, and serial busy state at line 243, so unauthorized changes to those conditions can create false or missing interrupt notifications. Withholding the request at line 243 can delay servicing and prevent an interrupt-driven system from progressing its transfers.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could manipulate the enable or engine-status conditions so the interrupt is falsely asserted or withheld while service is required.

conceptual assets.information: The sensed one-wire level is sampled from the external data line and returned as a diagnostic status bit. Software may depend on it to observe the current one-wire line state.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The sensed level comes from the one-wire input sampling path at line 296 and is exposed in the bus response at line 158, so modifying either path can make the reported line state incorrect.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter the sampled line value or its read-back path so software observes a false one-wire level.
